cells.tense: You are here, and what is ending is ending at the pace it actually takes.
cells.ask: Lay out the one thing you are actually keeping, next to what is going out, and name where each goes.
cells.core:
You know who you are in this, and it's not a performance for the room. Something is finishing around you — a way of being needed, a shape of a day, an arrangement you've been the one holding — and you are letting it finish without rushing or dragging it out. That's the whole of it. You don't have to prove you're fine with it. You're just not pretending it isn't happening.
People can feel that from you. They come to a room where something is being put down and nobody is being blamed for putting it down. The part to watch is that this reads easily as a gift and you can start giving it away. Keep one place where it's just yours. Let the ending land as its own thing, not as a lesson anybody around you is getting.
cells.sheetLine: Something is ending and you're letting it end without making it a speech.
cells.place: Where what has ended is being let end

cells.tense: You are already living past the ending, in a version of it that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that has not finished yet and leave it alone for a full day, on purpose.
cells.core:
You are pushing the new shape before the old one has finished. Somewhere ahead of you is the version where this is clean, settled, already the story you'd tell — and you're living there, so present mess reads as something to hurry. The hurry is what's costing you. What's actually ending can't be speed-run. It ends when it's ended. You know you're fine with it, and you want the people around you to know it too, and that wanting puts a performance on top of the ending instead of a door.
Nobody can move through a performance of being finished. Let the light come off whatever comes next rather than off your grip on the present. The clearing does its own work.
cells.sheetLine: You are rushing an ending so it will look finished.

cells.tense: You keep standing at something that has already closed behind you, waiting for the room to open again.
cells.ask: Put a date on one thing you're still tending, and check whether it's carried you or you're carrying it.
cells.core:
Something ended and you kept it going by shrinking. Not dramatic — small. Turning down the light, keeping quiet about what you can do, calling it being modest. You took what was yours to be and shrank it so nobody would have to adjust. That was a way of being kind to a situation that needed it, and it worked, and it is still running.
The problem isn't that the ending was wrong. It's that you're past the door and still holding it open for somebody who isn't coming. Nothing here needs you to make yourself smaller. The next shape doesn't start where the old one stopped working; it starts where you choose something with both hands. Pick one thing, say yes to it plainly, and let the yes be enough.
cells.sheetLine: You turned your own light down to make an ending easier.

cells.tense: You are already the one letting this end, and you keep talking like the ending is something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you ended on purpose, and call it your decision when you say it.
cells.core:
You've already started it. Something is being cleared — a habit, a role, a way you used to spend a day — and you're the one doing the clearing. You stopped, or you didn't answer, or you walked out of the noise. But you tell it like it happened on its own. Things ended, circumstances changed, the timing was just off.
What's in front of you now, this hour, is something you get to meet, not something to be managed. You don't have to announce it or have a theory about it. Just notice that the person making the call was in the room the whole time, and stop saying otherwise. Whatever comes next is entering on your watch. Let it land as yours.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is yours. You've been calling it circumstances.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person is mid-shedding, clearing, or ending anything — the record only says the card landed in Transformation, not what they are leaving. Reader's likely objection: 'I'm not ending anything, I'm just tired of a few things' — so every cell locates the mechanism in a moment they can put down, never in a story about what must end. The ask survives being wrong because each one is a small act with a day on it, not a verdict about their life; if the read misses, they still have a thing they can do or not do. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: any version of 'you are shining and don't know it' said as praise — flattery about radiance is the writer preening, so that line is kept out or aimed somewhere a camera could see.
